summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with HCV- and alcohol-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and depression was admitted for worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and a new-onset retro-orbital headache. She exhibited signs of hepatic encephalopathy, including asterixis and mental fogginess, likely exacerbated by opioid-induced constipation. Imaging revealed a hemorrhagic brain metastasis in the right temporal lobe, confirmed by MRI, prompting involvement of Radiation Oncology for stereotactic radiosurgery planning. Abdominal pain was attributed to constipation and preexisting necrotic lymphadenopathy. She was stabilized with lactulose, rifaximin, and a revised pain regimen including hydromorphone and tramadol with senna. Goals of care were discussed, and a MOLST form was signed for DNR/DNI. She was discharged home with follow-up in Radiation Oncology, Liver Clinic, and Palliative Care.
